rationale: Required delay loop handles pending APCs, relative/absolute deadline recalculation, timer insertion and context switch; stack-swap setup is already disabled for Xbox. No safe unmeasured wait shortcut.

name: KeDisconnectInterrupt
backend: XeKeDisconnectInterrupt -> Xbox eight-slot interrupt shadows + native i386 IRQ object
rationale: Eight-slot lookup resolves native state; driver-owned tombstones refuse disconnect even when detached. Native lifecycle and ownership are mandatory; no profitable general rewrite supported.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeEnterCriticalRegion
backend: KeEnterCriticalRegion -> Native APC-disable counter and pending delivery
rationale: Decrements current thread KernelApcDisable after a compiler barrier. Leaf cost is required APC inhibition, already minimal.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: MmGlobalData
rationale: Export is an aligned zero-initialized 32-byte placeholder for Xbox-shaped MM internals; there is no callable cost. Must preserve size/address and honest absent contents.
risk: Data ABI size/address and writable placeholder must remain stable.

name: KeGetCurrentIrql
backend: KeGetCurrentIrql -> Active UP PIC PCR IRQL / pending interrupt dispatcher
rationale: Active non-MINIHAL implementation reads PCR Irql. The later MINIHAL PASSIVE constant is inactive. One field read needs no change.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeGetCurrentThread
rationale: Returns the current native thread embedded Xbox shadow address; constant PCR/thread access and pointer arithmetic, no lookup table.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeInitializeApc
backend: XeKeInitializeApc -> Xbox title KAPC adapter / native APC insertion + trampolines
rationale: Writes the 40-byte public KAPC fields and overrides mode/context when no normal routine. Allocation is deferred until insertion; already efficient for initialized-but-unused APCs.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeInitializeDeviceQueue

rationale: Initializes type/size/list/busy in Xbox 12-byte queue; SARCH_XBOX omits the NT spinlock. Necessary structure writes only.

name: KeInitializeDpc

rationale: Delegates to KiInitializeDpc; Xbox branch stamps public structure state and callbacks. No allocation or queue traversal at initialization.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeInitializeEvent
backend: KeInitializeEvent -> Dispatcher event/mutant/semaphore wait and wake
rationale: Sets event type/size/state and self-links wait list, intentionally leaves unrelated header fields alone. Replacing with full memset would add work and modify observable bytes.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeInitializeInterrupt
backend: XeKeInitializeInterrupt -> Xbox eight-slot interrupt shadows + native i386 IRQ object
rationale: Allocating lookup scans up to eight occupied plus eight free slots, zeros native storage and invokes native initialization. Occasional lifecycle work preserves the 112-byte public buffer and driver-owned guards.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeInitializeMutant

name: KeInitializeQueue

risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeInsertDeviceQueue

name: KeInsertHeadQueue

name: KeInsertQueue
backend: KeInsertQueue -> Native KQUEUE concurrency / packet and waiter lists

risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeInsertQueueApc

Count pool transactions, peak retained blocks, lookaside hits/misses and title callback/delete counts; capped warm serial traffic should avoid repeated pool calls, cold/burst fallback must match ownership. Include allocation OOM and teardown/relaunch. Claim timing improvement only beyond observed variation; otherwise report verified work reduction.

rationale: Returns the published 3374488-Hz constant in the 64-bit ABI. Leaf constant return is already minimal.

rationale: Reads shared system time using high/low/high consistency retry; concurrent clock changes require the retry, and no pool allocation is involved.

name: KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel
backend: KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel -> Active UP PIC PCR IRQL / pending interrupt dispatcher
rationale: Reads/writes PCR Irql and returns previous value; already a minimal UP PIC raise helper.

name: KeReleaseMutant

rationale: Dispatcher exclusion validates owner/abandon behavior, updates recursion/state, unlinks final ownership, wakes waiters and restores APC disable. Already constant unless required wake fanout.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeReleaseSemaphore

rationale: Checks semaphore adjustment for limit/overflow under dispatcher exclusion, publishes count and wakes waiters when transitioning from zero. Wait=TRUE lock handoff and precise exceptions must remain.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeRemoveByKeyDeviceQueue
backend: KeRemoveByKeyDeviceQueue -> Native intrusive device queue + Xbox IRQL-only exclusion
rationale: Already checks last key to wrap to head, otherwise scans to first qualifying key under queue exclusion. O(n) interior lookup is imposed by intrusive public list without safe extra metadata; no candidate absent workload evidence.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeRemoveDeviceQueue
backend: KeRemoveDeviceQueue -> Native intrusive device queue + Xbox IRQL-only exclusion
rationale: One locked head removal or busy-clear when empty. Constant work with required Inserted update.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeRemoveEntryDeviceQueue
backend: KeRemoveEntryDeviceQueue -> Native intrusive device queue + Xbox IRQL-only exclusion
rationale: One queue exclusion, Inserted test and direct unlink. No scan; returning prior state and clearing insertion marker are essential.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeRemoveQueue
backend: KeRemoveQueue -> Native KQUEUE concurrency / packet and waiter lists
rationale: Tracks previous/current associated queue and concurrency, takes a ready packet directly or installs wait/timer/APC state. Context switch cost is required; cannot replace with polling.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeRemoveQueueDpc
backend: KeRemoveQueueDpc -> Native Xbox KDPC UP queue
rationale: Active Xbox branch masks interrupts and directly unlinks Inserted DPC/corrects queue depth; already no native DpcData lock path.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeResetEvent
backend: KeResetEvent -> Dispatcher event/mutant/semaphore wait and wake
rationale: Dispatcher exclusion captures previous state and clears state; constant leaf work plus potentially necessary dispatcher exit.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeRestoreFloatingPointState
backend: KeRestoreFloatingPointState -> i386 NPX hardware state save/restore and nonpaged pool
rationale: Validates saved thread/NPX IRQL, restores hardware FPU state and frees two allocations paired with save. Coalescing internal storage can remove one free while keeping validations and full FPU restoration.
risk: medium; internal ownership change and larger single contiguous pool request can alter fragmentation/failure profile.

Count nonpaged alloc/free calls (two to one) and allocated/requested bytes including alignment. Inject OOM, fragmented pool and wrong-thread/IRQL diagnostic cases in isolated guests; compare successful state bytewise and error behavior. After implementation, execute actual baseline/candidate export paths with identical compiler, xemu configuration, immutable inputs and guest ISO; alternate order for at least seven paired trials, retain all samples and report median/variation. Claim timing improvement only beyond observed variation; otherwise report verified work reduction.

name: KeResumeThread
backend: KeResumeThread -> Native thread state + UP dispatcher/APC exclusion
rationale: APC exclusion decrements suspend count and only takes dispatcher handling when the final suspend and freeze counts vanish. Existing inactive fast branch is present.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

backend: KeRundownQueue -> Native KQUEUE concurrency / packet and waiter lists
rationale: Detaches queued entry list in constant work and walks associated threads to clear Queue before dispatcher exit. Per-thread writes are required to avoid dangling ownership.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rationale: Allocates a save-context block and a separate FX_SAVE_AREA plus alignment padding, saves previous owner state, initializes FPU and returns an opaque context. Two allocation transactions are avoidable through one combined allocation; hardware state preservation is mandatory.
risk: medium; internal ownership change and larger single contiguous pool request can alter fragmentation/failure profile.
measurement: Repeat 1000/10000 save/restore pairs at PASSIVE/APC/DISPATCH and nest depth 1/2/8 while exercising x87/SSE register/control state and a second thread NPX owner. Count nonpaged alloc/free calls (two to one) and allocated/requested bytes including alignment. Inject OOM, fragmented pool and wrong-thread/IRQL diagnostic cases in isolated guests; compare successful state bytewise and error behavior. Claim timing improvement only beyond observed variation; otherwise report verified work reduction.

name: KeSetBasePriorityThread
backend: KeSetBasePriorityThread -> Native thread state + UP dispatcher/APC exclusion
rationale: Computes saturation/clamp/base-relative priority and quantum under dispatcher/thread coordination, only moving ready state when priority differs. Arithmetic/queue updates are contract work.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSetDisableBoostThread
backend: KeSetDisableBoostThread -> Native thread state + UP dispatcher/APC exclusion
rationale: Uses atomic bit-test set/reset on DisableBoost and returns old flag. One atomic operation; no worthwhile source-level change.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSetEvent
backend: KeSetEvent -> Dispatcher event/mutant/semaphore wait and wake
rationale: Already returns immediately for a signaled notification event with Wait=FALSE. Other cases require dispatcher state/wake consumption and WaitNext handoff; no additional safe unchecked fast path identified.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSetEventBoostPriority
backend: KeSetEventBoostPriority -> Dispatcher event/mutant/semaphore wait and wake
rationale: Dispatcher exclusion either marks signaled, handles WaitAll through shared wake logic or directly unlinks/boosts one waiter. Special boost policy and WaitingThread output must stay intact.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSetPriorityProcess
backend: KeSetPriorityProcess -> Xbox process shadow / native KeSetPriorityThread
rationale: Xbox implementation updates process shadow base and current thread only for 1..15. Other title threads and public ThreadListHead are deliberately missing; this is a correctness divergence, not a speedup opportunity.
risk: Existing correctness/behavior limitation identified; optimization must not mask it. Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSetPriorityThread
backend: KeSetPriorityThread -> Native thread state + UP dispatcher/APC exclusion
rationale: Dispatcher/thread coordination changes priority and ready-list position with quantum/boost resets. Existing equality test avoids actual rescheduling; mutable priority cannot be cached outside exclusion.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSetTimer
backend: KeSetTimer -> Native timer buckets / due-time and expiry dispatcher
rationale: Only supplies Period=0 to KeSetTimerEx. Wrapper has no redundant scan/allocation to eliminate; shared timer insertion handles cost.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSetTimerEx
backend: KeSetTimerEx -> Native timer buckets / due-time and expiry dispatcher
rationale: Cancels existing insertion, computes absolute/relative due time, signals immediate expiry or inserts into ordered timer bucket, and exits dispatcher. Bucket scans are required by current public intrusive structure; preserve deadline/tie/DPC behavior.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeStallExecutionProcessor
backend: KeStallExecutionProcessor -> i386 HAL calibrated delay loop
rationale: Active i386 HAL stall multiplies requested microseconds by calibrated PCR factor then performs decrement loop; zero exits immediately. Removing iterations weakens minimum-delay hardware contract.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSuspendThread
backend: KeSuspendThread -> Native thread state + UP dispatcher/APC exclusion
rationale: APC exclusion checks maximum suspend count, queues suspend APC only when transitioning into suspended state or adjusts semaphore if APC already present. Required counting and asynchronous suspension, no safe bypass.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSynchronizeExecution
backend: XeKeSynchronizeExecution -> Xbox eight-slot interrupt shadows + native i386 IRQ object
rationale: Eight-slot lookup routes through native IRQ synchronization, excludes driver teardown while using borrowed pointer and preserves tombstones. No-shadow direct callback is an existing behavioral limitation, not an optimization to generalize.
risk: Existing correctness/behavior limitation identified; optimization must not mask it. Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeSystemTime
rationale: Live KSYSTEM_TIME wall clock maintained with system-time updates; data-only export must retain published layout.
risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

name: KeTestAlertThread

rationale: APC exclusion consumes alert flag or marks UserApcPending if user list exists. Required state ordering for alertable waits; no repeated scan or allocation.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeTickCount
rationale: Live KSYSTEM_TIME tick counter; ordinal aliases existing native storage, no extra callable adapter.
risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

name: KeTimeIncrement
rationale: ULONG nominal clock increment initialized by KeSetTimeIncrement; shared clock contract data, no call cost.
risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

name: KeWaitForMultipleObjects
backend: KeWaitForMultipleObjects -> UP dispatcher / native waits, timer, APC and context switch
rationale: O(Count) WaitAny/WaitAll checks and intrusive wait-block setup handle recursion/abandon, timeout and APCs under dispatcher coordination. Xbox stack-swap path is already disabled; mutating wait states forbid a cached signaled shortcut.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KeWaitForSingleObject
backend: KeWaitForSingleObject -> UP dispatcher / native waits, timer, APC and context switch
rationale: Already satisfies signaled objects or owned mutants without sleeping; otherwise handles APC/timeout/timer/context switch. Preserve WaitNext atomic handoff and late APC delivery.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KfRaiseIrql
backend: KfRaiseIrql -> Active UP PIC PCR IRQL / pending interrupt dispatcher
rationale: Active PIC helper reads old PCR Irql and stores requested value; no hardware mask writes on raise. MINIHAL stub is inactive.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KfLowerIrql
backend: KfLowerIrql -> Active UP PIC PCR IRQL / pending interrupt dispatcher
rationale: Active PIC lower saves flags, disables interrupts, publishes level and dispatches pending software IRQs, including necessary PIC mask writes. Hardware accesses and pending interrupt ownership cannot be skipped.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: KiBugCheckData
rationale: Five-word bugcheck parameter storage written by fatal diagnostic backend; exact layout and parameters matter, no callable cost.
risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

name: KiUnlockDispatcherDatabase
backend: KiExitDispatcher -> UP dispatcher / native waits, timer, APC and context switch
rationale: Alias reaches KiExitDispatcher: processes deferred ready state, either lowers promptly or switches to already-selected NextThread and delivers pending APCs. UP dispatcher acquire/release already avoids an SMP lock.
risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

name: LaunchDataPage
rationale: Mutable launch-data-page pointer consumed across warm-reset chainload; pointer publication/persistence is required data behavior.
risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

name: MmAllocateContiguousMemory
rationale: Unbounded form forwards to Ex; active NXK_MM_PHYS clamps title RAM below 64 MiB and excludes the GPU region for generic requests. Tracking scans/grows a table; the supply already skips failed pages in a descending aligned search and may copy/rehome live frames. Required bounds, zeroing policy, pin immovability, ownership and TLB retargeting outweigh speculative alternate scans; protect/cache alias limitations are existing behavior, not optimization.
risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

name: MmAllocateContiguousMemoryEx
rationale: Unbounded form forwards to Ex; active NXK_MM_PHYS clamps title RAM below 64 MiB and excludes the GPU region for generic requests. Tracking scans/grows a table; the supply already skips failed pages in a descending aligned search and may copy/rehome live frames. Required bounds, zeroing policy, pin immovability, ownership and TLB retargeting outweigh speculative alternate scans; protect/cache alias limitations are existing behavior, not optimization.
risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

name: MmAllocateSystemMemory
rationale: Wrapper attempts the demand-mapped system aperture then falls back to tagged NP pool on NULL. The hole scan redundantly reads absent PDEs per page; candidate skips proven-free spans without changing first-fit or mandatory zeroed backing. Per-page PFN lock transitions are not removed without a latency study.
risk: Low to medium: page-count and PDE-boundary arithmetic; empty small requests already perform few checks, and backing-page zeroing can dominate.
measurement: Run the actual baseline and candidate kernel implementation through the exported ordinal in the same release compiler/xemu 128-MiB configuration and immutable guest ISO; at least seven paired trials, alternating order; retain all samples, median and variation. Check exact outputs/state and operation counters first; claim timing improvement only beyond observed variation. No measurements were executed in this read-only audit. Use 1/16/1024/1025/4096-page requests and holes crossing PDE boundaries, fully present fragmentation, and absent spans after occupied regions. Compare exact VA and zero-filled bytes, pool fallback and failure unwind. Count PDE/PTE reads and lock duration. An all-absent 4096-page search performs 4096 baseline PDE occupancy reads versus four PDE-span reads in the proposal; backing work is unchanged.

name: MmClaimGpuInstanceMemory
rationale: Query sentinel reads claim state; mutation rounds/clamps at most 16 instance-memory pages, reserving newly claimed PFNs with relocation or returning shrinking pages. Physical GPU window and padding are fixed; no avoidable bulk work beyond required per-page ownership moves. Existing failure reporting/claim semantics must not be replaced with success. XbDbg trace is absent in release; DBG=1 diagnostics add work.
risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

name: MmCreateKernelStack
rationale: Rounds nonzero stack bytes, allocates tagged pool backing, performs two atomic page counters and returns top-of-stack. Shared pool-window search candidate may reduce allocation scanning; retain stack shape and counter ownership, and do not use movable-stack relocation assumptions.
risk: Low to medium: scan boundary mistakes can change returned VA or false-fail allocation; fast empty-window cases may see no benefit.
measurement: Run the actual baseline and candidate kernel implementation through the exported ordinal in the same release compiler/xemu 128-MiB configuration and immutable guest ISO; at least seven paired trials, alternating order; retain all samples, median and variation. Check exact outputs/state and operation counters first; claim timing improvement only beyond observed variation. No measurements were executed in this read-only audit. Allocate actual pool runs of 1/2/4/16/256/1024 pages; construct dense, alternating, free-prefix-before-blocker and full-window patterns; compare chosen VA/failure and freed-page accounting. Count tested bits/bitmap loads, candidate probes, PFN operations and lock duration. A 4096-page map with occupied every 256th page and Count=256 gives an illustrative source-model 493696 bit checks versus 4096 with conflict skipping; this is a counted algorithm model, not a measured kernel speedup.

name: MmDeleteKernelStack
rationale: Validates base/limit ordering, rounds their difference, frees the derived tagged base and atomically subtracts two page counters. Required allocation lifetime and per-page unmap/TLB work dominate; adapter is constant-sized. Checked pool frees also record last-freer attribution, unlike release.
risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

name: MmFreeContiguousMemory
backend: NxpHeapFree -> pin check / persistence clear / supply return; NxkMmFreeRestored
rationale: Finds a live tracking entry under NxContigLock, checks every page for pins, then clears persistence and returns the run; pinned free is intentionally inert and tracking survives. Fallback handles restored warm-reset runs. Scans are concrete but adding an index would change concurrency/lifetime metadata without demonstrated frequency.
risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

name: MmFreeSystemMemory
rationale: NULL returns zero; aperture free walks caller-sized PTEs, skips already-free entries, clears mapping, returns each frame and reloads CR3. Fallback frees tagged pool and returns rounded page count. Zero-size/no-mapping flush avoidance needs separate proof and timing; required visibility invalidation is preserved.
risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

name: MmGetPhysicalAddress
backend: Static aliases / nxmm MmGetPhysicalAddress in xb/mm/fault.c
rationale: Range checks return masked KSEG0 RAM PA or identity WC/MMIO PA; all other VAs use active nxmm page-table walker in fault.c. Static shortcuts are already constant-time; caching translations could go stale under relocation/unmap.
risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

name: MmIsAddressValid
rationale: Three range tests shortcut static windows, then walk PTEs for pool/title mappings. No redundant allocation or scan. System-VA aperture shortcut is broad relative to demand mapping and should be treated as an existing correctness concern, not extended by optimization.
risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

name: MmLockUnlockBufferPages
rationale: Validates zero/overflow then holds the PFN lock across full-buffer preflight and apply. Preflight accounts for aliases atomically, but BeginPinBatch clears RAM-sized scratch even for one page; touched-PFN cleanup can remove that unrelated cost while retaining two-pass ownership checks. A fixed-page-budget bulk reset on large prefixes avoids an additional large rejection cleanup translation pass; sparse cleanup is not a universal speedup.
risk: Medium: stale scratch after any rejection violates the next preflight; prove zero-on-entry/exit in all branches. Sparse rejection adds at most the fixed page-budget of extra translations. Large-prefix bulk fallback retains one baseline-sized clear and avoids the extra cleanup walk, but moving the clear and adding mode branches still require timing; no universal speedup is claimed.
measurement: Run the actual baseline and candidate kernel implementation through the exported ordinal in the same release compiler/xemu 128-MiB configuration and immutable guest ISO; at least seven paired trials, alternating order; retain all samples, median and variation.
